findings.text: follow-on: the re-anchored releases_at path is unguarded. reckon/budget.py:3022 _re_anchor_releases_at is added code that no test asserts: tests/test_a_paced_window_reanchors_at_lift_end.py contains no assertion on releases_at (grep for it returns nothing), so a regression that mis-solves the release instant on the re-anchored line, or drops it, leaves the suite green. The held verdicts the negative control exercises (test lines 260, 277, 425) guard the held/unheld decision only. The branch is reachable in production: reckon/budget.py:3231 reads releases_at whenever a re-anchored group is held.

follow-on: the manifest's gate-command fields carry angle-bracket placeholders. manifest.md:15 'tests:' and manifest.md:21-22 baseline_suite.command / after_suite.command read 'scratch/arm_resume.sh <base_tree> base' and '... <worktree> head' with literal <base_tree>/<worktree> placeholders rather than the literal command with absolute paths, which the manifest contract forbids; the gate receipt can still be recovered from the log's own '# command:' header, and the arms' failure_ids are also abbreviated to five ids where scratch/arm_base.log and scratch/arm_head.log each carry seventeen, so the recorded lists understate the suite. Neither affects the code gate.
